### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Bardet-Biedl syndrome 16  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10671)

**Proposed mechanism:** SDCCAG8 (HGNC:10671) —DISRUPTS→ Endosomal trafficking and autophagy regulation (GO:0005758); Endosomal trafficking and autophagy regulation (GO:0005758) —LEADS_TO→ Renal abnormalities (HP:0000077); Endosomal trafficking and autophagy regulation (GO:0005758) —LEADS_TO→ Obesity (HP:0005101). Loss-of-function mutations in SDCCAG8 disrupt endosomal trafficking and autophagy regulation, leading to the shared phenotypes of renal abnormalities and obesity seen in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SDCCAG8 with a gain-of-function mechanism or in distinct genes for each disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs749174301)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SDCCAG8 in these distinct conditions could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting endosomal trafficking or autophagy that benefit patients with either disease.

#### 2. lissencephaly due to LIS1 mutation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)

**Proposed mechanism:** PAFAH1B1 (HGNC:8746) —DISRUPTS→ LIS1-dynein interaction and microtubule dynamics; SDCCAG8 (HGNC:29405) —DISRUPTS→ Cell migration and neuronal development; LIS1-dynein interaction and microtubule dynamics —LEADS_TO→ Cell migration and neuronal development; Cell migration and neuronal development —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal neuronal migration (HP:0012405); Cell migration and neuronal development —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in PAFAH1B1 disrupt the LIS1-dynein interaction and subsequent microtubule dynamics, which are critical for cell migration and neuronal development. Similarly, mutations in SDCCAG8, while potentially acting through a distinct but related pathway, also impact cell migration and neuronal development. Both disruptions converge on impaired neuronal migration and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in PAFAH1B1 or SDCCAG8 in individuals with neither MONDO:0013326 nor MONDO:0011830, or conversely, the absence of mutations in these genes in individuals with both conditions, would weaken this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in the coding regions of PAFAH1B1 or SDCCAG8 that are associated with either disease would falsify the proposed causal link.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of these neurodevelopmental disorders, particularly the role of LIS1 in microtubule dynamics and neuronal migration, could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at ameliorating developmental deficits. Identifying common pathways may also allow for repurposed treatments.
